title: The owner of a deleted memory reads only its tombstone; every other observer reads nothing; views are stable under other scopes and restart

invariants.statement: The owner of a governed-deleted memory reads tombstoned, no current fact, no events, no rejected values, the version its deletion recorded, and no identifier or text of the deleted generation, live and after restart.
invariants.falsified_by: any identifier, text, event or rejected value, or a different version

invariants.statement: Another project reads the deleted memory byte-identically (ids and timestamps folded) to an id nobody wrote: history, a value probe, recall by logical reference, and historical recall, live and after restart.
invariants.falsified_by: any difference from the unknown-id result

invariants.statement: The owner's deleted view does not change when another project re-creates, corrects and deletes the same id, and each deleting scope reads exactly the version its own deletion recorded (the two generations have different lengths, so a view serving the largest or latest deletion would differ).
invariants.falsified_by: any field of the owner's view changing, or either scope reading the other's recorded version

invariants.statement: A memory derived from a deleted fact is withheld from public recall while a live derivation keeps its provenance.
invariants.falsified_by: the derived-from-deleted memory or the deleted fact surfacing, or the live derivation lost

invariants.statement: A re-created generation's public history carries only its own events and nothing of the former generation in any payload; another scope's refused attempt leaves no trace in it.
invariants.falsified_by: an event, identifier or text from the former generation or from a refused attempt

invariants.statement: No receipt on a governed-deleted id -- committed, refused or policy-parked, from any writer -- and no history of a new generation carries the former generation's version count.
invariants.falsified_by: a before_state, after_state, snapshot or history version continuing the former count

clauses.clause: Versions are generation-relative ... After a governed deletion of the head the id reports `0` to any writer, a re-creation's receipt reads `v0 -> v1`, and the former generation's count never reaches the new one; the owner of the deleted generation still reads the version its deletion recorded (`tombstoned`, DUR-DEL-001).

A governed-deleted generation is closed. At the fact level (`dispute` of a tombstoned fact by its uuid, a governed pruning of one of its versions, the adapter's delete of a member of a deleted lineage) the answer is `already_deleted`; at the facade's logical-reference level (`forget`, permanent `forget`, `correct`, `dispute` by `target_reference`) the former owner reads the bare `fact_not_found` result, because the reference has no visible head. Either answer is the same whether or not another scope has since re-created the id, and neither moves or reads the live generation [...] The one further governed act is the escalation of a reversible pruning to a permanent deletion by a writer eligible for that generation: it keeps the tombstone's `deleted_at`, recorded version and lineage, erases the content, and neither reads nor moves a live generation another scope holds.
